title: Claw win plays two victory jingles on the same frame (j_treasure then game_over's j_victory)
repro: Win a prize at the claw: _win() calls sfx("j_treasure") and immediately game_over(lines), which plays sfx("j_victory") because tickets (10+) >= _good_tickets() 10. Two different fanfares stack in different keys. Confirmed by probe: Music._last_sfx after _win(0) holds j_treasure and j_victory in the same frame.
fix: Give ArcadeGame.game_over a way to skip its result jingle (e.g. var over_jingle_done := false, set true by a game that already played its own sting), or drop the j_treasure in ArcadeClaw._win and let game_over's j_victory be the one sting.

title: Skee-Ball's average game ends on the 'battle lost' sting (uses default _good_tickets 15)
repro: ArcadeSkee has no _good_tickets override, so the default 15 applies. Its own comment says a casual game pays ~1.2 tickets per crystal (fee 10 -> ~12 tickets), so an ordinary game plays j_battle_lost (a defeat sting from the battle kit) every time. Same for any game near the line; Whack (12), Stack (12), Gallery (20) each pick their own.
fix: Override _good_tickets() in ArcadeSkee (about 10, i.e. break-even on the fee), and for a below-par round play a softer neutral 'round over' cue (e.g. j_page or a new j_arcade_over) instead of j_battle_lost in ArcadeGame.game_over; keep j_battle_lost for real defeats.
audio_needed: optional: a short neutral arcade 'game over' jingle (j_arcade_over) from ace_kits

title: Claw: aim servo re-triggers in stuttering bursts, and the claw's drop/lift/carry are silent
repro: Hold left/right at the claw: `int(phase_t*10) % 3 == 0` is true for 6 frames in every 300 ms, so with Music's 70 ms dedupe servo.ogg (0.47 s) starts twice ~80 ms apart, then pauses, over and over: a flanged stutter that ties up 2-3 of Music's 6 voices. After A, the claw descends, grabs, lifts and carries to the chute for several seconds with no machine sound at all (only cloth on grip). servo.ogg is also very quiet (I -27.4 LUFS, peak -16 dB) under arcade_hall.
fix: Give ArcadeClaw its own AudioStreamPlayer (process ALWAYS, bus SFX) looping a motor whir while the claw moves (aim with dir != 0, drop, lift, carry), stopped/faded in grab/release; or at least trigger servo on the edge of a move press and every 0.45 s while held. Lift servo level a few dB (tools/sfx_soften.py or volume on the player).
audio_needed: optional: a loopable claw motor whir (CC0 servo/motor loop) if servo.ogg doesn't loop cleanly

title: Villager opponent's rolls use wrong, ungraded sounds (bowl_roll for 1-6 pins is louder than the strike; a gutter plays the UI 'nope' buzz)
repro: Challenge a villager (Bowling versus mode). In phase "opp" each shown roll plays Music.sfx("pin_crash" if v>=7 else ("bowl_roll" if v>0 else "nope")). bowl_roll is a 1 s rolling-ball clip at I -14.9 LUFS, louder than pin_crash (-18.6), so a weak 3-pin ball sounds bigger than a 9-pin one; 10 pins never uses pin_strike; 0 pins plays the error buzz the player hears for their own mistakes.
fix: Reuse RecAudio's grading: pin_tap (1-2), pin_crash (3-9), pin_strike (10), bowl_gutter or bowl_pit (0); ideally via a small RecAudio helper (e.g. RecAudio.opp_roll(v) returning the name) and played a little quieter than the player's own lane (it's the next lane).

title: Prize Music Box ('plays a little tune') and the 900-ticket home Jukebox ('a real jukebox') are silent props
repro: Buy rp_music_box (150 tickets) or rp_jukebox (900 tickets, the epic prize) at the prize counter and go home. RecCenter.dress_house only places a sprite (jukebox_b at [1,5], music_box on the trophy shelf); nothing plays, A on them does nothing, and house music stays 'house'. The item text promises a tune / a real jukebox.
fix: In dress_house register a thing (or House interaction) for both: the home jukebox steps through RecAudio.RECORDS like the rec one (needle sfx + toast) and stores run.flags.home_juke so House.area_track/GameMap.area_track returns it inside the house; the music box plays title_musicbox (exists in audio/music) as the house song while chosen (A toggles), or a short spot loop when the player is near. Keep it per save; add a small test (house area_track honours the choice).
audio_needed: none (title_musicbox and all records already exist)

title: Claw and Skee-Ball (in-room machines) cut the jukebox record you just picked and swap to arcade_hall
repro: Pick a record on the rec jukebox (it plays all day, both floors), then step to the claw machine or the skee lane: ArcadeGame._ready -> _start_music() plays arcade_hall (neither ArcadeClaw nor ArcadeSkee overrides it), so the record crossfades out for the length of the game and back in after. They are physical machines standing in the room, not screens with their own soundtrack. Confirmed by probe (tools/probe_c6_12_music.gd): with jukebox_oldie playing, claw and skee_ball both switch to arcade_hall and restore jukebox_oldie on close.
fix: Override _start_music() in ArcadeClaw and ArcadeSkee to keep the room's song (no-op, or Music.set_duck(-3) while open, restored in close). Keep arcade_hall for the video cabinets.

title: One 91 s arcade_hall loop serves the picker, Stack, Whack, Duck Pond (and claw/skee today) and is also a jukebox record: heavy repetition, no level change
repro: Play a few rounds of Crystal Stack (several minutes) or alternate cabinets: the same 91 s loop restarts each time; Stack's level-ups ('LEVEL n · FASTER!') and Whack's final seconds have no musical lift. Only Block Jumper has its own chiptune (arcade_jumper).
fix: Render 3 short cabinet loops with ACE (e.g. arcade_stack: tense puzzle chiptune; arcade_whack: bouncy carnival; arcade_duck: fairground organ), import with tools/ace_batch.py, and override _start_music() per game falling back to arcade_hall when Music.has_track is false. Optional: Stack lifts Music pitch_scale slightly per level (or switches to an _fast variant from level 5), Whack plays a short 'hurry' sting at 5 s left.
audio_needed: 3 ACE loops: arcade_stack, arcade_whack, arcade_duck (60-90 s, -16 LUFS, seamless)

title: Crystal Stack top-out: 3 s cave_in still roaring when the results jingle starts 1.1 s later
repro: Stack out: _top_out plays cave_in (3.0 s), TOPOUT_SECS is 1.1, then game_over plays j_victory/j_battle_lost over the remaining 1.9 s of rumble.
fix: Use a shorter 'stack out' cue (thud / block_fall) or stop the voice before game_over; or set TOPOUT_SECS to ~1.6 and fade the rumble (play it through an owned AudioStreamPlayer you can fade).

title: Block Jumper: every landing plays the heavy 0.6 s 'thud' (louder than the jump), and coin runs repeat one fixed-pitch clink
repro: Play any Block Jumper level: ev "land" -> sfx("thud") (I -15.6 LUFS, 0.6 s, a combat/drop impact) fires on every landing, several times a second on stairs/platform runs, while the jump itself is a 0.11 s pop. coin is excluded from Music's pitch drift, so a row of 6-8 coins is the same stamped clink.
fix: Land on a light cue (step_wood, or thud played through a quieter path e.g. a dedicated AudioStreamPlayer at -10 dB, only when the fall was longer than ~0.25 s); jump stays pop. For coins keep a short streak counter (reset after 0.6 s without a coin) and raise pitch_scale by a semitone per coin up to +7 via a small ArcadeGame.sfx_pitch(name, pitch) helper.

title: Solo bowling always ends on the j_victory fanfare, even a 20-point gutter game
repro: Bowl a solo game badly: _game_over plays j_victory because result.won defaults to true without an opponent.
fix: Solo: j_victory only for a new best or >= 100 (or a mark-heavy game), else a lighter j_page/sparkle; versus keeps won/lost. Optionally a cheer (clap) on a new best.

title: Whack-a-Grump helmet 'CLANK' uses the same soft 'hit' as a normal bop
repro: Bop a helmet grump once: the screen says CLANK but sfx("hit","thud") is the same as a knock-out hit, so the armour has no audible feedback.
fix: Play sfx("anvil", "sword_clash") (both exist in audio/sfx) on the armoured first hit, keep 'hit' for the knock-out.

title: Results card is silent beyond one jingle: no ticket-dispense count, no new-best or milestone cue
repro: Finish any cabinet: '+N tickets' appears static with the result jingle; a NEW BEST banner and an 'Arcade milestone' toast (ArcadeHub.set_milestone) get no sound of their own, so the best moments sound like any round.
fix: In ArcadeGame: count won_tickets up over ~0.8 s on the results card with a soft repeating tick (scroll_tick at rising pitch, or a new ticket_feed cue) and play j_secret (exists) once for new_best; ArcadeHub.set_milestone plays j_skill/j_secret through Music when it toasts (dedupe with the new-best cue in the same frame).
audio_needed: optional: ticket_feed (short mechanical ticket chatter, CC0) for the count-up

title: Take-to-take loudness jumps in arcade/rec sounds: servo takes differ by 20 dB (one near-silent), cash 9 dB, drop 8 dB, pin_crash 6 dB
repro: Max 50 ms RMS per take: servo -34.2 vs servo_2 -14.1; cash -17.1/-15.4/-24.7; drop -12.8/-16.2/-20.6; pin_crash -12.2/-14.1/-18.3; coin/gem/cash_pickup ~4-5 dB. Music.sfx picks a take at random, so the claw motor is inaudible on half its triggers, the snack-bar 'cash' and soda 'drop' jump in level, and a 9-pin villager ball can sound smaller than a 2-pin tap. SOFTEN_LOG shows the cause: sfx_soften's lowpass + high shelf on bright takes (servo: rms -15.4 -> -28.9, cash_3: -16.5 -> -24.8) with gain capped at +6 dB.
fix: In tools/sfx_soften.py add a take-levelling pass: after filtering, bring every <name>_2/_3 to within ~2 dB of the group's median RMS (allow more than +6 dB make-up when the filter removed it, keep TP <= -1.5 dB); rerun with --force on servo, cash, drop, pin_crash, coin, gem, cash_pickup (rm before write: files are hardlinked). Add a check in tools/sfx_audit.py that fails when takes of one name spread > 6 dB.

title: Full-screen games don't adjust the mix: room beds keep playing under cabinets/bowling, and the pause card doesn't dip the music (Ambience resets any duck every 0.5 s)
repro: Open a cabinet downstairs or bowl upstairs: Ambience (PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS) keeps the arcade_floor bed (other cabinets' attract chirps) / rec_alley bed (other balls rolling) at full room level under the game's own sounds; only spot sounds stop while paused. Pause Stack/Whack (B): only menu_open plays; music stays full. Any Music.set_duck from a screen would be undone because Ambience._evaluate calls mu.set_duck(duck) (0 indoors) every 0.5 s. Confirmed by probe: downstairs before a game rec_alley=-22/arcade_floor=-19; 5 s into Crystal Stack (tree paused, music arcade_hall) beds unchanged.
fix: In Ambience._evaluate: when Hud.modal_rect has size (a full-screen screen is open) scale room beds down ~8 dB (keep a faint room tone). Give Ambience an extra duck input (e.g. static var screen_duck := 0.0 added to its computed duck) so ArcadePause can set -6 dB while paused and clear it on resume/close, instead of calling Music.set_duck directly.

title: Jukebox: the record crossfades in on the same frame as the 2.4 s needle drop, and every press restarts the song
repro: Press A on the rec jukebox: _jukebox calls mus.play(t) and mus.sfx("juke_needle") together, so the needle crackle sits on top of the new song's first second instead of leading into it; tapping again to browse restarts a new crossfade each time.
fix: Play juke_needle first, dip the old song (fade 0.4) and start the record ~0.8 s later (get_tree().create_timer(0.8).timeout -> mus.play(t, 0.3)); ignore a second press for ~1 s (flag) so browsing doesn't stack needles/crossfades.

title: Gangster arc: in-game arcade coins/points rustle like banknotes (Money maps every 'coin' sfx to cash_pickup)
repro: Gangster arc, play Block Jumper: every pixel coin collected plays cash_pickup (paper bills); same for Skee 50-pointers, the golden duck in Duck Pond and the golden grump in Whack. Those are game points, not money. cash_pickup also isn't in Music.sfx's no-pitch-drift list (coin is), so it wobbles in pitch.
fix: Keep sfx("coin") only for inserting the coin (ArcadeGame.start); for in-game pickups use an unmapped cue (e.g. new 'arcade_coin' chiptune blip, or 'gem'/'sparkle' fallback) so both arcs hear an arcade sound. Add cash_pickup/cash to the no-drift list in Music.sfx.
audio_needed: optional: arcade_coin (8-bit coin blip, 2-3 takes) via ace_kits or CC0

title: Looped lane rumble includes the file's fade-out: a slow ball hears a ~0.25 s dropout as the loop wraps
repro: bowl_rumble.ogg (4.0 s) ends in a fade (last 250 ms window -42 dB vs ~-31 body). RecAudio._start_roll loops it with loop_offset 0.5 but plays to the file end, so a soft ball (speed 230 + slow-motion stretch near the pins, ~3.9 s on the lane) or any ball long enough to wrap hits a hole in the rumble just before the pins.
fix: Don't rely on the file end: in _start_roll, if the roll is still going at ~3.6 s, restart _roll at 0.5 s (seek) or crossfade into a second player; or re-render bowl_rumble with a seamless loop body (tools/make_rec_audio.py, crossfade the tail like ace_import.seamless).

title: Skee-Ball reuses the heavy bowling roll (single take, 1.05 s, loudest cue in the set) for a 0.4-0.6 s ramp roll, 9 times a game
repro: Each throw: sfx("bowl_roll") (one take only, I -14.9 LUFS, > 0.45 s so no pitch drift) while _roll_time() is 0.40-0.62 s; the bowling-ball rumble runs on over the hop 'pop' and the landing 'thud' and is identical on all nine balls.
fix: Play the roll through an owned AudioStreamPlayer and stop/fade it when phase leaves 'roll' (pitch_scale up with shot_p so a hard throw sounds faster), ~4 dB quieter; or add a light wooden-ball roll cue (skee_roll, 2-3 takes).
audio_needed: optional: skee_roll (small wooden ball on a ramp, 2-3 takes, CC0)

title: Web build: no rec/arcade song is prefetched, so the jukebox announces a record that doesn't play yet and short cabinet games can end before arcade_hall/arcade_jumper arrive
repro: Phone/web build (all 12 rec/jukebox songs are streamed per data/music_stream.json; PREFETCH lists hold none of rec_center, bowling_alley, arcade_hall, arcade_jumper, jukebox_oldie). First visit: the town song carries on inside the rec until rec_center (~1.4 MB) downloads; opening the claw/a cabinet keeps the room song until arcade_hall arrives; pressing the jukebox toasts '"Nickel Record"' while the old song keeps playing for several seconds.
fix: On entering the rec (RecCenter enter hook) queue Music prefetches for rec_center/bowling_alley (arc's house song), arcade_hall, arcade_jumper and the next jukebox record (a small Music.prefetch(list) that feeds _prefetch_next before the static lists). In _jukebox prefer the next record already in Music._streamed/user://mcache and show the toast when the song actually starts (or 'The jukebox whirs...' until then). Test with Music.force_stream (tools/music_stream_test.gd pattern).

title: Bowling new best: j_victory plays at game over in the screen and again when you leave it
repro: Bowl a new personal best solo: Bowling._game_over plays j_victory; tapping out, RecCenter's lane result (rec_center.gd ~817) plays j_victory again with the score toast (coin otherwise).
fix: Let the screen own the result sting (it knows best/won); RecCenter plays only a ticket cue (coin / a ticket_feed) with the toast. If the bowling solo jingle is reworked (see the solo-ending finding) keep them in one place.

title: Upstairs plays 'pins_near' crashes and a busy-lanes bed even when every lane is visibly empty; rec spots are single takes from random spots around the player
repro: Visit the bowling floor in the morning (no villager on a lane: RecCenter.lanes_taken() empty): RecAudio.SPOTS rec_up fires pins_near every 9-24 s and the rec_alley bed (rolling balls) runs at -10, though RecDecor shows four idle lanes and real villager balls already make their own panned lane_sound. Ambience._spot places it 60-140 px from the player in a random direction (can come from a wall), and spot_pins_near / spot_cabinet_win / spot_pins_far have one take each, so the same 2 s clip repeats. Confirmed by probe (tools/probe_c6_12_beds.gd, day 10 10:00): lanes_taken()={} yet beds rec_alley=-10.0 dB, arcade_floor=-27.0.
fix: Make RecAudio.spots/beds take the lane state: drop pins_near when no lane is taken and scale rec_alley by taken lanes (e.g. -22 dB empty, -10 dB with 2+ bowlers); downstairs keep pins_far only if someone is bowling. Let Ambience spots pick _2/_3 takes and a +-5% pitch, and give RecAudio spots an optional anchor (lane head / cabinet wall) instead of a random ring.
audio_needed: optional: 2 extra takes each of spot_pins_near, spot_pins_far, spot_cabinet_win (tools/make_rec_audio.py)

title: Duck Pond: knocking a toy duck plays the combat 'hit', a frog plays the UI error 'nope'
repro: Hit a duck: sfx("hit","thud") (the sword/fist impact used in fights); hit a frog: sfx("nope") (the menu refusal buzz). Nothing says fairground: no tin ding, no squeak, no croak.
fix: Duck: a tin target ding (anvil at higher pitch via a pitch helper, or a new gallery_ding) plus optional squeak; golden duck keeps its sparkle/coin cue (see the gangster coin finding); frog: a croak (Ambience has spot_frog in audio/amb; or a short frog sfx) instead of nope.
audio_needed: optional: gallery_ding (tin target), duck_squeak, frog_croak short sfx (CC0)

title: 1200-ticket home Arcade Cabinet prize is an inert sprite (no game, no sound)
repro: Buy rp_arcade_cab and go home: dress_house places props/arcade_cab_1 at [1,7]; A does nothing. The most expensive decor prize can't be played.
fix: Register a thing on it in dress_house that calls ArcadeHub.open(map, "") (the picker: free play at home could skip fees and tickets, or pay tickets as usual), plus a soft attract-mode spot loop near it. Pairs with the home jukebox/music box finding.
needs_tom: Should home cabinet plays cost/pay tickets or be free practice?

title: Result jingles (j_victory, j_treasure, j_battle_lost, j_buy) play on top of the cabinet/room song at full level, in a different key
repro: Finish any cabinet, strike in bowling, buy at the prize counter: the j_ sting (I about -14 to -16 LUFS, -4 dB voice = ~4 dB over the -24 dB music bed) lands over arcade_hall / the jukebox record with no dip, so two keys and tempos clash for 2.5-2.9 s.
fix: In Music.sfx, when name begins with 'j_' and the sting is > 1 s, dip the music player ~7 dB for the sting's length and ease back (separate from Ambience's duck: add a _sting_duck term that set_duck/_tw_in respect, since Ambience re-applies set_duck every 0.5 s).
